messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer on Private (VPC) reports intermittent failures when connecting through their corporate proxy. App calls Redwood via CONNECT to tls Redwoods endpoint, but the tunnel is closed immediately. Symptoms: client shows 'read ECONNRESET' and our side sees TLS handshake aborted. Posting repro + captures below.

customer-bob: Here's the minimal repro: from their VM (behind corp proxy) `curl -x http://corp-proxy:8080 -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/models`

customer-bob: curl output: 
```
* CONNECT corp-proxy:8080 HTTP/1.1
> CONNECT api.redwood-inference.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.internal:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.0.0.5) port 8080 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

maria: They also captured a short pcap. From the pcap the proxy returns a 200 then immediately sends a RST after a few dozen bytes of the ClientHello. Proxy also injects `Proxy-Authenticate: NTLM` in other flows.

ryan: Interesting. Could be the proxy is doing NTLM auth/inspection and trying to MITM TLS, then closing when it doesn't like the SNI or cipher list. Do we have the raw ClientHello bytes?

customer-bob: Attached small tcpdump excerpt (hex) showing ClientHello truncated at ~512 bytes. The ClientHello contains our server name: `api.redwood-inference.internal`.

sre-jess: A few quick checks: 1) Is the proxy actually configured for CONNECT tunneling for port 443 (some infra appliances only allow CONNECT but then still terminate and re-proxy)? 2) Is there an egress allowlist blocking the destination IP? 3) Are there transparent L7 devices doing protocol detection and rewriting the ALPN/SNI?

infra-ankit: We often see enterprise proxy appliances that present 200 then do TLS inspection by issuing their own TLS handshake — they expect to act as MITM. If the client uses TLS 1.3 0-RTT or extensions they don't understand, proxy might drop. Also NTLM flows can cause the proxy to close non-authenticated CONNECTs.

maria: Customer says developers did not configure proxy auth for their service account; but their browsers work (they do interactive NTLM). The app uses a service principal and non-interactive flow so the proxy rejects it.

ryan: Actionable repro steps for the customer: 1) Run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.internal:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -ign_eof` from the VM bypassing proxy (if possible) to confirm server responds. 2) From the VM with proxy enabled, run a verbose CONNECT via netcat to inspect headers. 3) Capture a pcap of the whole TCP handshake + TLS ClientHello and share.

sre-jess: Also check whether the proxy rewrites the CONNECT line — some appliances require `CONNECT host:443 HTTP/1.0` or include `Proxy-Authorization`. Example bad vs ok: 
```
# bad (gets proxied/terminated)
CONNECT api.redwood-inference.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.internal
Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive

# ok (tunnel pass-through on some proxies)
CONNECT api.redwood-inference.internal:443 HTTP/1.0
Proxy-Authorization: <ntlm token>

``` 

infra-ankit: Workarounds until customer updates proxy: - Configure the VM/service to send Proxy-Authorization with NTLM/Kerberos if allowed. - Bypass proxy for Redwood endpoints via no_proxy/Egress rule to go direct (requires network change). - Use a non-inspected port if enterprise firewall allows it (eg 8443) and we can expose an alternative endpoint (we can discuss with infra).

customer-bob: We can't change corp proxy policy quickly. Can Redwood do anything server-side? E.g., accept IP-only connections (no SNI) or downgrade TLS?

maria: Short answer: we don't control their proxy. On our side we can offer suggestions: - Provide an IP-based endpoint to avoid SNI mismatch (requires their firewall rules to allow the IP). - Offer a dedicated egress/static IP (Private/Dedicated customers can request static egress from Redwood, helps with allowlists). - Temporarily enable a plain TCP echo endpoint for diagnostics.

ryan: I'll check whether we can expose a temporary IP endpoint for this customer's VPC + add a note to support docs about NTLM/CONNECT pitfalls. Also adding an internal runbook: 'If proxy injects Proxy-Authenticate: NTLM -> ask customer to capture full HTTP exchange and advise on no_proxy or NTLM config'.

sre-jess: For troubleshooting ask them to grep pcap for `Proxy-Authenticate` and `Proxy-Connection` headers and share sanitized excerpt. If the proxy is terminating TLS, you'll see two separate TLS sessions (client->proxy, proxy->server). If proxy is tunneling, you'll see one uninterrupted TLS session.

customer-bob: I'll collect the pcap and the proxy config lines and DM them to @maria. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #23415 linked to this thread and escalated to Infra. SLA: 4h.

maria: Thanks — looping in @ryan for follow-up on exposing IP-based diagnostic endpoint. I'll keep thread updated. :eyes:
